title: Donald Trump sexually assaults model Amy Dorris
description_short: Donald Trump sexually assaults model Amy Dorris
description_medium: Amy Dorris told The Guardian that Donald Trump assaulted her at the 1997 U.S. Open, including forcing his tongue into her mouth and groping her in his private box. She said she was unable to get free. Trump denied the allegation through his lawyers. The Guardian reported that Dorris shared her account with people close to her at the time.
description_long: Amy Dorris told The Guardian that Donald Trump sexually assaulted her at the U.S. Open in New York on September 5, 1997. She said the encounter began when she left the bathroom in Trump’s private box, where he forced his tongue into her mouth, groped her and held her tightly enough that she could not get away. Dorris was 24 and attending with her then-boyfriend, Jason Binn. She gave the Guardian a ticket and photographs from the days she spent with Trump in New York. The report also said her mother, a friend, a therapist and other friends corroborated that she had described the alleged incident to them. Trump denied through lawyers that he had ever harassed, abused or behaved improperly toward Dorris. The account is an allegation, which Trump disputes; the article does not report a legal finding about it. The timeline labels the event September 6, while the Guardian’s report dates it September 5. That one-day discrepancy should be resolved before the entry is treated as a date-specific incident record.

preserved_fields.title: Donald Trump sexually assaults model Amy Dorris
preserved_fields.description_short: Donald Trump sexually assaults model Amy Dorris

notes: Needs context: the linked Guardian report dates the alleged incident September 5, 1997, while the timeline record is dated September 6, 1997; its headline also states the disputed allegation as fact although Trump denied it.
Proposed correction: align the date to the Guardian report and frame the title as Dorris’s allegation, retaining Trump’s denial.

title: Trump: Michael Caputo works with Russia to improve Putin's image in the U.S.
description_short: Trump: Michael Caputo works with Russia to improve Putin's image in the U.S.
description_medium: In 2000, Michael Caputo worked in Moscow for Gazprom Media on a public-relations campaign about Vladimir Putin, according to the supplied timeline. After returning to the United States, he started a firm in Miami at Roger Stone’s suggestion. Caputo later joined Trump’s 2016 campaign; the chronology does not show that his earlier Russian work was done for Trump.
description_long: The supplied timeline says Michael Caputo began working in Moscow in 2000 for Gazprom Media, a subsidiary of Russia’s state-owned energy company, on a public-relations campaign intended to improve Vladimir Putin’s image in the United States. It says Caputo returned later that year and, at Roger Stone’s suggestion, moved to Miami Beach and started his own public-relations agency. Caputo later worked for Donald Trump’s 2016 campaign, but the gap between those roles does not establish that the Moscow assignment was for Trump or connected to the campaign. The entry’s source pages could not be opened in the earlier review, so the employer, the campaign’s specific work and its timing remain unverified here. A useful account can preserve the reported chronology while distinguishing Caputo’s later campaign role from his earlier job in Russia. It should not imply a Trump campaign connection without evidence that links the two.

preserved_fields.title: Trump: Michael Caputo works with Russia to improve Putin's image in the U.S.
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: Michael Caputo works with Russia to improve Putin's image in the U.S.

notes: Needs context: the earlier review reported HTTP 403 for both linked pages, so the Moscow employment and campaign description remain supported only by the supplied timeline text.

title: Donald Trump talks to New York magazine about Jeffrey Epstein
description_short: Donald Trump talks to New York magazine about Jeffrey Epstein
description_medium: A 2002 New York magazine profile quoted Donald Trump saying he had known Jeffrey Epstein for about 15 years and calling him a “terrific guy.” Trump also said Epstein liked beautiful women, “many of them on the younger side.” The remarks document how Trump described their acquaintance at the time; they do not establish what he knew about Epstein’s later crimes.
description_long: In a 2002 New York magazine profile, Donald Trump described Jeffrey Epstein as a “terrific guy” and said he had known him for about 15 years. Trump also remarked that Epstein liked beautiful women, “many of them on the younger side.” The profile presented Epstein as cultivating an image of a quiet, solitary man who did not drink or use drugs, while also describing his active social life. Trump’s comments placed the two men in a social relationship dating back, by Trump’s account, to the late 1980s. They are relevant as a record of what Trump said publicly about Epstein before Epstein’s later criminal cases. The interview does not establish what Trump knew about Epstein’s conduct, whether he knew of allegations made by others, or how their relationship changed afterward. The entry is about the 2002 remarks and the acquaintance Trump described, not a finding about knowledge or complicity. Those distinctions keep the documented statement separate from claims that the supplied account does not establish.

preserved_fields.title: Donald Trump talks to New York magazine about Jeffrey Epstein
preserved_fields.description_short: Donald Trump talks to New York magazine about Jeffrey Epstein

notes: The descriptions are limited to Trump’s reported statements in 2002 and do not infer his knowledge of Epstein’s later crimes.

title: Trump: Felix Sater: Mafia, Trump, FBI, CIA, and Money Laundering
description_short: Trump: Felix Sater: Mafia, Trump, FBI, CIA, and Money Laundering
description_medium: Felix Sater worked for Bayrock Group, which partnered with the Trump Organization on Trump SoHo, and later cooperated with U.S. authorities after pleading guilty to racketeering in a stock-manipulation case. The supplied draft distinguishes those facts from Sater’s later intelligence claims and does not establish that Donald Trump took part in Sater’s crimes.
description_long: Felix Sater pleaded guilty in 1998 to racketeering in a $40 million stock-manipulation scheme and later cooperated with U.S. authorities. He worked for Bayrock Group, a partner in the Trump SoHo development, and promoted real-estate projects with Donald Trump. Sater’s criminal case and business relationships are separate matters: the available reporting does not show that Trump participated in the stock scheme or Sater’s claimed intelligence work. A New York Times account said Trump did not know Sater well and was surprised to learn about his criminal past. The entry’s date, June 7, 2006, is described in its source notes as a post date rather than a documented event date. The documented link in the account is a real-estate partnership, not evidence that Trump shared responsibility for Sater’s separate criminal conviction or his alleged intelligence contacts. Without a dated event and support for the FBI and CIA claims in its title, this record reads as a profile, not an event record.

preserved_fields.title: Trump: Felix Sater: Mafia, Trump, FBI, CIA, and Money Laundering
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: Felix Sater: Mafia, Trump, FBI, CIA, and Money Laundering

notes: Needs context: the source notes say June 7, 2006 was selected as a timeline posting date, not an event date; the linked New York Times article returned HTTP 403 and the supplied record does not substantiate the title’s intelligence claims.
Proposed correction: make the entry a sourced profile or identify a dated event, and retain intelligence allegations only with direct supporting records.

title: Federal Ban on Media Coverage of Protests - Press Freedom Elimination and Information Control
description_short: Federal Ban on Media Coverage of Protests - Press Freedom Elimination and Information Control
description_medium: The Kettering Foundation’s review describes Project 2025 proposals that could affect press independence: limiting permanent White House media access, placing Voice of America under closer State Department control and ending federal funding for public broadcasting. Those proposals are not evidence of an implemented ban on protest coverage or criminal penalties for journalists.
description_long: Donald Trump implemented federal bans on media coverage of protests by revoking press credentials for journalists who reported on demonstrations while using Project 2025's plan to eliminate journalist access to public protests and criminalize news reporting that covered political dissent or civil rights demonstrations. The systematic press freedom elimination represented Trump's strategy to control information about government resistance by preventing journalists from documenting protest activities while using federal law enforcement to arrest reporters who attempted to cover demonstrations, effectively eliminating independent media coverage of political opposition. The media ban included denying press access to protest sites while establishing federal penalties for journalists who reported on civil rights demonstrations, political activism, or government resistance activities, creating information blackouts that prevented Americans from learning about dissent or opposition to administration policies. Trump's press control violated First Amendment protections for journalism while eliminating public access to information about democratic participation and civil rights activities, transforming protest coverage from protected journalism into criminal activity subject to arrest and prosecution. The media coverage ban created what press freedom advocates called systematic elimination of independent journalism about political dissent while establishing government control over information that enabled authoritarian rule without media scrutiny or public accountability. The press freedom destruction represented Project 2025's vision of media controlled by government authorization rather than constitutional protection, eliminating journalism that had historically exposed government overreach while ensuring Americans could not learn about resistance to authoritarian policies through independent media coverage and factual reporting.
subcategory: Media Coverage Prohibition and Press Freedom Elimination
